about: Youth sports and the town: what the leagues pay to use the fields, the funds that money lands in, and what the boards have said about the arrangement since 2014.

conclusions.basis: sources/town-ledgers/account-details/field-rental-receipts-fy2024-fy2026-lysa.xlsx, every row; the extract beside it in sources/data.
conclusions.claim: Lunenburg Youth Soccer paid the schools $39,074 for field use in FY2024–FY2026, in 7 receipts.
conclusions.detail: The district’s business office answered a records request in September 2026 with a workbook of 7 receipts: a date, an amount and the payer’s name each, grouped by fiscal year as the district groups them. One receipt carries the accounting system’s own record — a cash receipt referenced 996437, described “THES RENTAL/FIELD RENTAL 2023/”. Amounts as printed; nothing here is computed from them except the sums.

total.unit: paid by Lunenburg Youth Soccer for field use, FY2024–FY2026

conclusions.not_shown: What the fields cost to keep, what any other league pays, or what the receipts were for by field and by season — the workbook lists dates and amounts, not invoices. A figure a person typed, not a printout from the books (rule 13a): the fund’s own journal would confirm each line.

see.label: What school sports cost, and who pays

conclusions.so_what: By fiscal year as the district lists them: FY2024 $6,728, FY2025 $23,308, FY2026 $9,038.

conclusions.basis: sources/town-ledgers/fund-balances/special-revenue-fy2026-p09.xlsx, the row for fund 1306, columns REVENUE, EXPENDITURE and FUND BALANCE; credits print negative and are shown here as amounts.
conclusions.claim: The School Facilities Use fund took in $18,670 in FY2026 through March and holds $71,559.
conclusions.detail: The town’s FY26 special-revenue report, a printout from its accounting system as of the end of March, carries the fund by number and name with its revenue, expenditure and available balance. Youth soccer’s three FY2026 receipts, $9,038, are 48% of the $18,670 the fund had taken in by March. The fund’s journal — which would list every payer — is not in the archive.

revenue.unit: into the School Facilities Use fund, FY2026 through March

conclusions.not_shown: Who else pays into it, and what the $12,354 was spent on. The report is balances, not transactions.

see.label: Every fund in the school money graph

conclusions.so_what: Fund 1306 is where field rentals land; it spent $12,354, and soccer’s receipts are 48% of the revenue.

conclusions.basis: The same FY26 report, the row for fund 1545; the Select Board recording of 3 May 2016 at 5,765 seconds, machine captions.
conclusions.claim: The Artificial Turf fund took in $45,000 in FY2026, the figure the 2016 plan adds up to.
conclusions.detail: The fund’s FY2026 revenue is $45,000, its expenditure $38,454, its available balance $69,390 — all as printed. That the $45,000 is $30,000 of cell-tower rent plus $15,000 from the soccer association is what the Select Board said the plan was in May 2016 (the recording, at 1:36:05), and it matches to the dollar. It is not established by any ledger the archive holds, which is why this card is a hypothesis: the receipt detail for fund 1545 would settle it, and would say whether the Bengals’ $7,500 is inside it or elsewhere.

revenue.unit: into the Artificial Turf fund, FY2026

conclusions.not_shown: Whether the arrangement is still what was described in 2016, or who signed it. A recording is a finding aid; the agreement itself is not in the archive.
conclusions.so_what: The 2016 plan as said: $30,000 a year from the cell tower, $15,000 from youth soccer. No ledger splits it.

grain: DOLLARS as three different documents print them — a MUNIS fund report (evidence), a records-request workbook (stated), and the annual reports’ schedules (transcribed, unreconciled) — kept apart on the page. Not what a field costs, and not what any league pays in total.
not_established: Who else pays into fund 1306, and how much: the fund’s journal detail (the report the archive holds for fund 1301) would list every receipt by payer.

What happened in FY2025: the fund stood at $3,010.67 on 30 June 2024 (the annual report) and at $65,241.82 on 30 June 2025 (the FY26 report’s opening balance), and nothing in the archive shows the year’s receipts and spending — the FY2025 special-revenue report would.
Whether the $45,000 a year in the turf fund is still $30,000 of cell-tower rent and $15,000 from youth soccer, as described in 2016, and where the Bengals’ $7,500 goes.
What the fields cost the town to keep. The schools’ grounds, custodial and utility costs are coded to no programme.

said.what: The turf replacement funding plan: $30,000 a year from the cell tower, $15,000 a year from Lunenburg Youth Soccer and $7,500 from the Bengals, “to achieve the goal of paying for the replacement of the field over its lifetime.”
“They cut us a check every season” — the Bengals and youth soccer paying a set fee toward the turf bond.
Field costs moved out of the operating budget into facilities-use funding, with the money received from youth soccer for the fields going there.
Reworking the facilities-use rates: “we were collecting a lot more from Lunenburg Youth Soccer than we might otherwise need.”
Youth soccer’s fall field requests “didn’t closely match up with what I expected as far as number of hours.”
“Are some of the organizations like Lunenburg Youth Soccer really associated with the public schools, or are they just Lunenburg-based sports organizations?”
“Talk to the presidents of Lunenburg Bengals, Lunenburg Youth Soccer Association, Lunenburg Youth Basketball Association — all these organizations that use our facilities.”
The athletic and facilities directors working out schedules with the leaders of youth soccer and the Bengals; a shared two-week look-ahead for every field.
$1,800 to replace soccer goals owned by youth soccer, taken when the league moved its practices off the high school fields.
